title: Κοχλίαι
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 172 (= Perry 54). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Γεωργοῦ παῖς κοχλίας ὤπτα· ἀκούσας δὲ αὐτῶν τριζόντων ἔφη· « Ὦ κάκιστα ζῷα, τῶν οἰκιῶν ὑμῶν ἐμπιπραμένων, αὐτοὶ ᾄδετε. »
sentences.tr: Geōrgou pais kochlias ōpta· akousas de autōn trizontōn ephē· « Ō kakista zōia, tōn oikiōn hymōn empipramenōn, autoi āidete. »
sentences.l: A farmer's boy was roasting snails; and having heard them squeaking he said: « O most worthless creatures, with your houses on fire, you yourselves are singing. »
sentences.n: ἀκούω takes the genitive of what is heard together with a participle for what it is heard doing: αὐτῶν τριζόντων. τρίζω is used of thin creaking, squeaking sounds — here the whistle of steam escaping the shells, which the boy chooses to hear as song. τῶν οἰκιῶν ὑμῶν ἐμπιπραμένων is a genitive absolute; the shells are the snails' houses, and ἐμπίπρημι is the verb used of setting a building alight. κάκιστα is the superlative of κακός in its moral sense, good-for-nothing rather than merely unlucky.

sentences.t: Ὁ λόγος δηλοῖ ὅτι πᾶν τὸ παρὰ καιρὸν δρώμενον ἐπονείδιστον.
sentences.tr: Ho logos dēloi hoti pan to para kairon drōmenon eponeidiston.
sentences.l: The story shows that everything done out of season is a thing to be reproached.
sentences.n: τὸ … δρώμενον is an articular participle, "the thing being done", with παρὰ καιρόν wedged inside the article's grip as a modifier. καιρός is the fitting moment rather than clock time, so παρὰ καιρόν is "beside the right occasion", untimely. No copula is written; ἐστί is left out, as regularly in these morals.
